deviations_from_adr: This IS the ADR-producing task (DIAGNOSE+DESIGN+BUILD in one). No prior ADR to deviate from. Deviated from the TASK-SUGGESTED option (а) (top-level userProfile key + kc-dev-setup) for a reasoned cause: empirically, KC 25 --import-realm does NOT honor a top-level userProfile key (import 400) nor a bare kc.user.profile.config realm attribute (ignored) — only the components.org.keycloak.userprofile.UserProfileProvider entry activates the profile. Since CI's kc job and fresh provisioning use ONLY --import-realm (never kc-dev-setup), the fix MUST live in components. kc-dev-setup step 5 additionally reconciles persistent stands from the same embedded config. Documented in ADR §2.1/§3.

diagnosis.symptom: A human account created from the product UI (POST /api/users -> createHumanUser) gets a login token with NO actor_type claim -> verifyClaims (src/http/auth.ts:302) returns 401 on EVERY request. Seeded fixture users work; UI-created users 401. Confirmed live on KC 25.0.6, realm choros, :8180.
diagnosis.root_cause: config/keycloak/realm-choros.json declared no user profile. KC 25.0.6 enables the declarative User Profile by default with unmanagedAttributePolicy=DISABLED, so actor_type is an unmanaged attribute and KC SILENTLY DROPS it on every admin-REST user create (POST /admin/realms/<realm>/users). The actor-type protocol-mapper then has no attribute to read -> no token claim -> 401. Seeded users escape only because realm-import writes attributes straight to the DB, bypassing profile validation.
diagnosis.proposed_target: config/keycloak/realm-choros.json (declare actor_type as a managed, admin-editable, options-validated user-profile attribute via the realm-import-native components entry) + scripts/kc-dev-setup.sh (reconcile the same config on persistent stands).

falsifiable.hypothesis: Declaring actor_type as a managed attribute in the KC declarative user profile makes the admin-REST create persist it, so the login token carries actor_type and verifyClaims passes.
falsifiable.prediction: After the fix: admin POST /users with attributes.actor_type=[human] -> GET user shows attributes.actor_type=[human]; ROPC token carries actor_type='human'; an invalid actor_type value is rejected 400.
falsifiable.refuted_if: The created user's stored attributes still show NONE, OR the token still lacks actor_type, after the profile declares actor_type admin-editable.

diagnosis.confirmation: Live, HIGH confidence. KC 25.0.6 (t-0633-keycloak-1, :8180, realm choros). BEFORE: admin POST /users 201 but GET user attributes=NONE; ROPC token actor_type=<<MISSING>>; seeded e-kravtsova token actor_type='human' (asymmetry reproduced). AFTER (declarative profile with managed actor_type applied): GET user attributes={actor_type:[human]}; ROPC token actor_type='human'; invalid actor_type=[superadmin] -> 400 error-invalid-value; seeded regression green; setUserEnabled PUT{enabled:false} -> 204 with actor_type intact. The EXACT committed realm-choros.json also proven through the KC import deserializer (import 201 -> profile active -> admin-create persists -> token actor_type='human', aud includes choros-api).
